label: Calf milk replacer
step: blend with whey, fat and vitamins, dry
note: Replacers of the 1950s and 60s were mostly skim milk powder; today most protein is whey (dried whey about 12 % protein, delactosed whey about 27 %, WPC about 35 %) or blends with vegetable protein. Replacers with whey protein do not clot with rennet, so clotting is no quality test any more.

about.text: A powder that replaces the cow's milk for a calf, so the cow's milk can be sold. It is made of dried skim milk and whey with added fat, vitamins and minerals, mixed with warm water and fed from bottle, bucket or automatic feeder.

how.text: Severely heat-treated skim milk does not clot in the calf's abomasum and gives diarrhoea, so skim for replacers is dried gently (low-heat powder).
